core_obligations: Reduce to the ph-sheaf condition (proof lines 22189-22204): the etale statement is the content of the etale description lemma, so it suffices to show that pi_S^{-1}F is a sheaf for the ph-topology; by the criterion for the ph-topology it is enough to produce, for every proper surjective V -> U over S, an equalizer diagram for (pi_S^{-1}F)(U) -> (pi_S^{-1}F)(V) => (pi_S^{-1}F)(V x_U V).

Rewrite the terms (proof lines 22205-22222): setting G = pi_S^{-1}F|U_etale, the values on V and on V x_U V are written as Gamma(U, f_*f^{-1}G) and Gamma(U, g_*g^{-1}G), and the two maps of the diagram come from two maps f_*f^{-1}G -> g_*g^{-1}G; hence it suffices to prove that G is the equalizer of those two maps of sheaves.

Check on stalks (proof lines 22223-22249): for a geometric point u of U with Omega = G_u, the proper-pushforward stalk lemma turns the two maps into the pullback maps H^0(V_u, underline Omega) -> H^0(V_u x_u V_u, underline Omega); sections coming from the two projections are constant on the fibres of the respective projection, so a section in the intersection of the two images is constant on all of V_u x_u V_u and therefore comes from an element of Omega, which is exactly the equalizer statement.
proof_roadmap: Quote the etale description and reduce the claim to the ph-sheaf condition.
Turn that condition into an equalizer statement for two maps of pushforwards.
Verify the equalizer statement on geometric stalks via the description of the stalk of a proper pushforward.

The proof (proof lines 22188-22249) quotes the etale description, reduces the claim to the ph-sheaf condition through the characterisation of ph-sheaves by equalizers along proper surjective morphisms, rewrites the terms as sections of two pushforwards, and verifies the resulting equalizer statement on geometric stalks using the description of the stalk of a proper pushforward. H2: one reduction plus one stalk computation, written out.
